clue.text: In decimals, tenths are so irrelevant

definitions.meaning: in a decimal such as 0.5 the tenths digit sits immediately next to the dot, so it is literally placed alongside the point
having no bearing on the matter in hand, off the subject

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: tenths are the first digit after the decimal point, so they sit right by it. The second is the everyday idiom for something that does not matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a remark that misses the issue under discussion, which is exactly what irrelevant means.

clue.text: On run? But they rent their trailer

indicators.note: rent is the past of rend, meaning torn apart, so the preceding words are ripped up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Fugitives are taunted: those who hire the caravan they tow have been warned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like paying for a hire, but it means torn: ONRUNBUTTHEY torn up gives the answer. 'their trailer' refers back to people on the run: the one who trails them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone paid a reward to track down fugitives is the person who follows, or trails, those on the run.

clue.text: Bar containing drop of liquid comfort

indicators.note: containing says the word for bar holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, as does save

indicators.note: a drop of something is a tiny bit, here just the opening letter of liquid

explanation.surface: A pub serving a little liquid as consolation.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing ointment, and figuratively anything that comforts or eases distress, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Wheel-checker's work unit included cleaner

indicators.note: included says the unit of work goes inside the wheel-checker

parts.note: a detent is a catch or pawl that checks the movement of a wheel in a mechanism
the erg is the CGS unit of work or energy

explanation.surface: Someone who inspects wheels is hired, part of a cleaning crew.
explanation.walkthrough: A detent is a mechanical catch that stops a wheel turning; ERG goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a cleansing agent, a substance that cleans, so cleaner is a fair noun synonym.

clue.text: Leaders of the record industry use many people hoping for success

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Music executives employ a large workforce, all wanting a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumph is a great victory or achievement, a straightforward synonym for success.

clue.text: Land of noble manner's uplifting to accept source of argument by both sides

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the turned word holds the following letters
in a down clue uplifting means the word is read from the bottom up, so backwards

parts.note: mode means manner or way, as in mode of address

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its opening letter

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left, the two sides

explanation.surface: A nobleman's estate is morally improved by taking in arguments from either side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns MODE into EDOM, which takes in A (start of 'argument') and RL (right and left).
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the territory or domain held by an earl, a nobleman, so it is a land of a noble.

clue.text: Tone down south's lacking much of the time

indicators.note: lacking says the word must do without the following letter

parts.note: to tone something down is to soften it
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Advice to moderate one's voice, as Southerners apparently don't.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens frequently happens much of the time, so the phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Badly done crown is singular coinage

indicators.note: badly signals the following letters are mangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A poorly made crown is a one-off coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coinage' suggests money next to 'crown', an old British coin, but here it means the coining of a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: A word made up for a single occasion is a one-off invention, a singular coinage in the linguistic sense.

clue.text: Group that's left in dark

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation for left goes inside the word for group

parts.note: a unit is a group, as in a military unit

explanation.surface: A band whose remaining member has been kept uninformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means without light, so it is an adjective synonym of dark.

clue.text: Annoying country that goes over scripture time and time again

indicators.note: goes over means covers, so the country wraps around the following letters

parts.note: Iran is a country in the Middle East
RI is religious instruction, the old school name for scripture lessons
a second T, another abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A nation that keeps revisiting religious texts is getting on someone's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: IRAN goes round RI and T, and another T follows. RI stands for religious instruction, the old British name for scripture lessons in school.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritant is something that annoys, and the word is also used as an adjective meaning annoying or irritating.

clue.text: Liner rattles about beyond the solar system

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: An ocean liner shakes violently, as if out in deep space.
explanation.definitionFit: Interstellar means between the stars, so it describes space beyond our own solar system.

clue.text: It may be proved by meteor fragments containing hydrogen

indicators.note: containing says the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside
fragments here is broken pieces, so the word meteor is shattered and its letters rearranged

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Scientists hope chunks of space rock carrying hydrogen will confirm a hypothesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a mathematical statement shown to be true by proof, so it is something that may be proved.

clue.text: Brown's gone away to prison

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: away suggests something gone astray, so the letters of gone are scattered

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown has disappeared off to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' reads as a name, but it is the colour DUN; the 's is a link meaning has.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a dark underground cell in a castle, a kind of prison.

clue.text: Formerly own ecstasy and speed

parts.note: hast is the archaic second-person form of have, so it means own as used formerly
E is the common abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: In the old days a person who had the drug would get a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste means hurry or quickness of movement, so it is a noun synonym of speed.

clue.text: Have form of vapour when climbing plant's type of Artemisia

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters rise from bottom to top, so they are read backwards

parts.note: to be something is to have the form of it, so this gives be
gas is matter in vapour form
the rush is a marsh plant; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A climbing plant gives off a mist, says the botanist describing wormwood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have form of vapour' reads as a description of mist, but split it: to be gas is to have the form of vapour. 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagebrush is the common name for several aromatic shrubs of the genus Artemisia found in western North America.

clue.text: For being one of 4

parts.note: the clue's first word, for, sounds exactly like the number four, so it is a word that sounds the same as another

explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as a statement about its own first word: 'For' is pronounced like '4', so it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A word pronounced the same as another but different in meaning, as for and four are.

clue.text: Oil of tropical plant turns up in slim case

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
in says the answer is found inside the clue's words

explanation.surface: Palm oil appears in a thin briefcase.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Oil of trop' backwards to find the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat, thin case for carrying papers or drawings, hence a slim case.

clue.text: Beats the endless spirit back with club

indicators.note: back says the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: to top something is to beat it, so beats gives tops

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter of the word the

parts.note: gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Drinking gin while tapping out rhythms on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beats' looks like a noun for rhythms, but it is the verb tops; 'the endless' supplies TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightspot is a nightclub, so club is a fair shortened synonym.

clue.text: Web-footed friends

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a mate is a friend

explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'friends', gives two pieces: PAL and MATE, both meaning friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Palmate describes a foot with webbing between the toes, as in ducks, so web-footed is a botanical and zoological synonym.

clue.text: Mounting one is overlooked in less sensible time frame

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means rising up the grid, so the letters are reversed
overlooked means left out, so the letter for one is dropped

parts.note: sillier means less sensible
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Climbing a ladder for an even sillier timeframe is ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time frame' looks like one phrase, but 'time' gives T and 'frame' is the definition; 'is overlooked' drops I, leaving SILLER before the turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice framework for supporting climbing plants, so it is a kind of frame.

clue.text: Floats in crests with zero gravity

indicators.note: with zero means none of the following letter remains

parts.note: ridges are crests, as of hills or waves
G is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: Something drifts on wave tops in weightless conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that rides at anchor floats on the water, so rides is a verb synonym of floats.

clue.text: Caustic stuff that keeps ball spinning rope in

indicators.note: spinning means turned round, so the whole thing is read backwards
keeps means holds, so the caustic stuff holds the ball inside

parts.note: quicklime is a caustic substance
an orb is a ball or sphere

explanation.surface: A corrosive substance keeps a ball rotating on a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rope in' looks like part of the surface's rope, but it is the definition: to involve someone in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to involve them in a conflict, much as to rope them in drags them into something.

clue.text: Derived from one that hid a king?

definitions.text: Derived from one that hid a king?

parts.words: Derived from one that hid a king?
parts.note: Charles II of England hid in a tree at Boscobel after losing the Battle of Worcester in 1651, the Royal Oak story

explanation.walkthrough: After defeat at Worcester in 1651, the future Charles II hid from his pursuers in a tree at Boscobel, famous in Britain as the Royal Oak.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaken means made of or coming from oak wood, the tree in which Charles II hid.

clue.text: Impose directions to make salicet salient

annotationWithheld.why: Impose directions to make salicet salient (7): the wordplay is a self-referential instruction, EN (directions) FOR CE turns salicet into salient, a reverse reading over a 4-word phrase that the grammar refuses (reversePhrase) and that no charade, anagram or cd tree can express honestly
annotationWithheld.clue: Impose directions to make salicet salient

clue.text: Fanatical attack to capture Baghdad's leader

indicators.note: to capture means to take in, so the attack holds the next letter

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

indicators.note: a word's leader is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A violent assault aims to seize the Iraqi capital's chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means extreme and zealous in opinions, as in a rabid supporter, so it means fanatical.

clue.text: No one applies for this post

definitions.text: No one applies for this post

parts.words: No one applies for this post
parts.note: post here is mail, not a job; nobody asks to be sent unsolicited advertising through the letterbox

explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like a job vacancy nobody wants, but it is mail that arrives unrequested.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsolicited advertising sent through the mail is something nobody requests, so no one applies for it.

clue.text: Reveal a believer's middle name

indicators.note: middle says the answer sits in the middle of the clue's words, spanning them

explanation.surface: Disclose a churchgoer's middle name.
explanation.definitionFit: A label is a name or tag given to something, and to label is to name, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Great wall of a chump from Eton?

definitions.text: Great wall of a chump from Eton?

parts.words: Great wall of a chump from Eton?
parts.note: the Great Wall of China is a world wonder; chump is slang for head, and a foolish upper-class man is said to have a weak jaw

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Great wall' as a wonder of China; a chump (slang for head) that lacks its chin makes the phrase. Eton is an elite English boarding school, standing for the upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for a feeble, foolish young man of the upper classes, such as an Old Etonian twit.
